questions.q: In the answer_question pipeline, what happens if every retrieved chunk scores below the score_threshold?
options: The function still calls the model with the low-scoring chunks anyway
The function returns the honest fallback immediately, with no re-ranking step and no model call
The function raises an unhandled exception
The function automatically increases top_k and retries forever
questions.explain: When nothing clears the score_threshold, the pipeline returns the Lesson 22 fallback directly, avoiding both the cost of re-ranking and the risk of a confident wrong answer from weak context.

questions.q: What does the rerank() call in the pipeline do, and where does it run relative to the score_threshold check?
options: It runs before the score_threshold check, on every query regardless of score
It replaces the embedding step entirely
It narrows the retrieved candidates down to the most relevant ones, and only runs after the score_threshold check has passed
It generates the final citations directly
questions.explain: Re-ranking only runs on chunks that already cleared the score_threshold check — there's no reason to spend a re-ranking call on candidates the pipeline has already decided aren't usable.

questions.q: In assemble_prompt, where does the citation instruction from Lesson 21 live?
options: In a separate API call made after the model responds
Folded directly into the same system prompt that carries the grounding instruction from Lesson 20
In the vector database's metadata filter
It is not included in this lesson's build at all
questions.explain: The capstone combines Lesson 20's grounding instruction and Lesson 21's citation instruction into a single system prompt, rather than treating them as separate steps.

questions.q: What does this lesson's build deliberately NOT yet include?
options: A re-ranking step
A grounded prompt
An abstention path
A measured evaluation score, or any tuning based on one
questions.explain: This lesson proves the pipeline works end to end structurally; measuring it with real evaluation metrics and tuning based on the results is left for Lesson 30.

questions.q: In the full round trip example, what makes a citation like '[1]' in the model's answer traceable back to a real source?
options: The re-ranker assigns citation numbers directly
The chunk's doc_id and page metadata, captured back at ingestion and carried through to the numbered context in the prompt
The vector database automatically generates citation text
The embedding model stores citation numbers in the vector itself
questions.explain: A citation is only traceable because the chunk was stored with source metadata (Lesson 16) that survives through retrieval and into the numbered context assembled into the prompt.
